newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly hold steady with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly hold steady with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly held steady Monday in lackluster trade, underpinned by stable crude, strong bunkers and firmer gas prices despite sagging East Coast utility demand, industry sources said.

"Utility demand is weak, but bunkers are strong. High sulphur feels a bit better and the rest is mostly stable," said one cash trader, noting firm East Coast city gate gas prices encouraged some fuel switching to cheaper resid.
New York Harbor physical one percent was unchanged at $14.25 a barrel, with May paper also steady in the $14.15-40 area. Traders said June paper remained quoted at $14.60-85.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour also was little changed at $15.25.
High sulphurs in New York remained steady, with 2.2 percent still talked around $14, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was unchanged to up slightly at about $14.50, while three percent also was flat to a little higher at $13.25-50.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
A Florida utility tendered Friday for 120,000 or 180,000 barrels of one percent or 1.8 percent for May 12-June 3 delivery. Bids are due Tuesday at 1100 EDT.

New York city gate swing gas prices firmed slightly Monday to the high-$2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.62 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, also gained two cents to the low-$2.20s/mmBtu, or $13.99 a barrel.
